_readme: Forward-looking runbook describing what an agent WOULD have to do to point this board at the real Tableau semantic layer. Nothing here has been executed. The app as shipped is mock-only: data/board.json is the single source of truth, there is no live tier in the fetch chain, and no code path in src/ reads this file. It exists so that 'switch this over to live data' is a documented procedure rather than an improvisation. Rewritten in full from docs/semantic-layer.md, which was written from a complete read of three real semantic-layer PDFs. The previous version of this file described a single invented 'Analytics Revenue SDM' with invented metric apiNames; that model does not exist. The real layer is two unrelated Tableau Next semantic data models plus a set of Tableau Cloud published datasources on a different server. Every apiName below that is not written as <TBD: ...> is quoted verbatim from those documents. Every identifier the documents do not definitively state is written as a <TBD: ...> placeholder on purpose — see guardrails.neverHardcodeIdentifiers. No apiName, workspace id, dashboard id, SDM id or datasource LUID has been inferred, completed or guessed here. SINCE THAT REWRITE, the business analyst who owns these semantic models has answered three of its findings directly, and her answers are authoritative over both this file and docs/semantic-layer.md — see provenance.modelOwnerCorrections. Two of them overturned conclusions this file had assembled entirely from verbatim quotations. The largest consequence is that THE FIVE YEAR TREND TAB CANNOT BE SOURCED (gaps.fiveYearTrendTabCannotBeSourced); the largest gain is that the segment tab's four-column set is sourceable after all, via a derived dimension the model owner supplied (portlets['seg-matrix'].derivedSegmentDimension).

Intraday Salesforce changes made after ~6 AM PT do not appear until the next day's extract. Both primary docs require an explicit 'as of' on any published brief.

slsSpecialistReporting.rowGrain: One row per opportunity-line record in the specialist forecast fact, per data source (Live / Snaps / Specialist Commit). One opportunity therefore recurs across data sources and across snapshots.
slsSpecialistReporting.defaultTimeframe: current fiscal year. 'Whenever a year timeframe is not specified, default to using the current fiscal year.' Only scope to a quarter when asked.
slsSpecialistReporting.mandatoryFilter: Is_Specialist_AE_Covered_Cleaned_clc = TRUE on every query without exception — see queryContract.alwaysOnFilters.slsSpecialistReporting.
slsSpecialistReporting.explicitlyExcluded: AOV, and all core-AE / standard opportunity reporting. SPEC §3: 'AOV / core-AE questions are out of scope.'
slsSpecialistReporting.rlsMechanism: Automatic. 'RLS is enforced automatically; data is pre-scoped to the entitled user's hierarchy.' Enforcing field Is_SFR_User_Entitled_clc (primary, marked visible but is plumbing), with Is_Entitled_User_clc as a hidden legacy path. Never surface either. This SDM has no Is_My_Data field at all: 'Never try to filter by a my data flag in this SDM — it doesn't exist.' Person scoping is an OR across Specialist_Level_04_User_Name … Specialist_Level_10_User_Name plus Specialist_User_Name, because a person appears at whichever level matches their role.

relationshipBetweenThem.joins: NONE. SPEC states the model is a single data object with no relationships, and neither document describes a join to the other. PULSE treats them as two tools in one kit and switches between them per card; it never joins them.
relationshipBetweenThem.theSingleMostConsequentialFact: The same word means two different numbers in the two models. ACV_clc (Forecasting) and ACV_Closed_Won_clc (Specialist) are not the same measure, are not reconcilable, and must never appear on the same tile. SPEC's fields represent the specialist's attributed share of a deal, which can differ from core opportunity values.

velocity.specialist: Specialist_V_clc — Velocity_clc is visible but discouraged ('defer to SPOX')

averageDealSize.specialist: Average_Deal_SIze_clc — the capital I typo is in the SDM and the apiName must match it exactly

scoping.specialist: no Is_My_Data at all; automatic RLS plus a hierarchy-level OR

relationshipBetweenThem.sharpestTrap: Coverage_clc is the CORRECT field in Sls_Forecasting_Metrics_Expanded and a HIDDEN, wrong field in Sls_Specialist_Reporting. A field name carried between models either silently changes meaning or silently returns nothing.
relationshipBetweenThem.segmentVocabularyDisagreement: Sls_Forecasting_Metrics_Expanded Segment10 carries ENTR, CMRCL, SMB, ESMB. Sls_Specialist_Reporting Derived_Macro_Segment carries CMRCL, ENTR, ESMB, PUBSEC plus null, and SPEC §12 warns explicitly that 'Segment is PUBSEC, not SMB.' SMB is a valid segment in one model and explicitly not a value in the other. Neither model has any counterpart to the board's 'growth' tier. This is load-bearing for the performance-by-segment tab — see portlets['seg-matrix'].
relationshipBetweenThem.segmentVocabularyDisagreementIsNotTheBlo: RESOLVED BY THE MODEL OWNER. This file previously recorded the board's four columns (ENTR, CMRCL, SMB, PubSec) as sourceable from NEITHER model, because Segment10 has SMB but no PUBSEC while Derived_Macro_Segment has PUBSEC but explicitly not SMB. That framing was wrong: it treated PubSec as a segment peer. The business analyst who owns these models states that PUBSEC IS AN OPERATING UNIT, not a segment, and that the board's four-way split is a DERIVED DIMENSION coalescing the two — 'IF OU = Public Sector then OU else segment end'. The two vocabularies still disagree about PUBSEC-as-a-segment-value, and that disagreement is still real; it just is not what blocks the tab. See portlets['seg-matrix'].derivedSegmentDimension for the full derivation and the one identifier it still needs.

connections.pathIsolation: Two servers, two schemas, two auths, two identifier systems. Tableau Next MCP targets a semantic data model by apiName and has no LUID anywhere in its surface. Tableau Cloud MCP targets a published-datasource LUID and has no SDM apiName. Do not mix tool calls or identifiers between them, and specifically do not attach the Cloud constraints below to a Tableau Next call, where they have no meaning.

tableauNextMcp.notes: This is the path both primary PDFs are written for. An SDM is queried by apiName through the Analytics Agent. There is no LUID in this path at all. This board's provenance model — certified measure, grain, lineage, RLS, freshness — maps onto the semantic-model surface here, which is why the app makes the argument it does. Every identifier must come from a live discovery call in the actual runtime environment on every run.

tools.list_semantic_models: Enumerate SDMs available to the caller. Returns id, apiName, label, description, dataspace, categories. The primary way to resolve a real SDM apiName.
tools.get_semantic_model: One SDM's profile including businessPreferences and lastModifiedDate. Read before querying.
tools.list_semantic_model_data_objects: Data objects/entities in an SDM: apiName, label, dataObjectName, filters[]. Also reports native dimension/measure visibility.
tools.list_semantic_model_relationships: Relationships between data objects: leftSemanticDefinitionApiName, rightSemanticDefinitionApiName, joinType, criteria.
tools.list_semantic_model_metrics: Governed business metrics/KPIs defined in an SDM.
tools.get_semantic_model_metric: One metric's full definition: measurementReference, timeDimensionReference, additionalDimensions, timeGrains[], filters[], aggregationType, isCumulative.
tools.list_semantic_model_calculated_measures: Calculated measures, with visibility, aggregationType and expression. This is where nearly every _clc field on this board lives.
tools.get_semantic_model_logical_view: A logical view's structure: semanticDataObjects[], semanticRelationships[], semanticUnions[], filters[].
tools.list_workspace_assets: Assets in a workspace: assetId, assetType, assetUsageType.
tools.search_assets: Search by keyword with optional type filter. Good first call when the workspace or SDM is unknown.

tableauCloudMcp.noLimitKeyClarification: The tool has no limit parameter, but the generated SQL does, and on the Tableau Next path the limit is expressed IN THE UTTERANCE. SPEC's ranking rule is 'ORDER BY <metric> DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10' for top-N. Conversely, for full-population pulls SPEC's Open Pipeline Misalignments pattern requires the phrasing 'return a table of ALL matching rows (do not limit results — request the full result set).' This is a phrasing requirement, not a parameter, and it is the mechanism acv-ae-fan depends on.

queryContract._note: Hard constraints, not guidance. Every item here has a named silent failure in guardrails.silentFailureModes.
queryContract.onlyQueryTool: analyze_data. SPEC §1, verbatim: 'Tableau Next MCP exposes one query tool: analyze_data (natural language). It generates SEMANTIC_VIEW(...) SQL internally. There is no field-level query API — the patterns below are prompt scaffolding + expected SQL, not a callable schema.'
queryContract.everyQueryIsAnUtterance: Every 'query shape' in this file is an UTTERANCE — a natural-language sentence that names the exact apiNames. The field names are not passed as parameters; they are named in a sentence so the agent generates the right SQL. The previous version of this file wrote query shapes as structured field lists, which the Tableau Next path cannot accept.
queryContract.resultsAreProse: analyze_data returns a natural-language answer or a table the caller must parse. Read the returned sentence and extract figures explicitly; do not regex-guess them. A compound comparison that comes back conflated or ambiguously rounded must be split into one utterance per period rather than parsed out of one prose answer.

discoveryIsMandatoryFirst.rule: Discovery is step 0, never assumed, every run. Only then analyze_data.
orderedSteps: 1. list_semantic_models / search_assets — resolve WHICH of the two SDMs (or a third, undocumented one) answers the question. They are not interchangeable; picking the wrong one silently answers a different question about a different population.

2. get_semantic_model — read businessPreferences. Both SDMs have baked-in rules that apply to every generated query whether or not you ask for them. One of them ('UP +') is wrong as a filter value and must not be copied out of the preferences into a query.

3. list_semantic_model_calculated_measures / list_semantic_model_calculated_dimensions / list_semantic_model_data_objects — confirm the apiName AND its visibility AND its aggregationType before naming it in an utterance.
4. analyze_data with 'list distinct values of <dimension>' for any enumeration you are about to filter on. Capture the generated SEMANTIC_VIEW(...) SQL.
6. Re-sort and re-check client-side. SPEC: 'After receiving results: re-sort the returned rows yourself … Do not rely on Tableau Next to sort — always re-sort in your own output.'
discoveryIsMandatoryFirst.visibilityIsNotOptional: Check field VISIBILITY at step 3. 'Only visible measures are queryable/presentable' (SPEC §6), and several fields this board wants are hidden: SFR_Pipe_Gen_Amount_clc (specialist pipegen), Coverage_clc in the Specialist model, and SFR_ID. Named working substitutes exist for the first two; a hidden field is not queryable and returns nothing rather than erroring.
discoveryIsMandatoryFirst.discoverySurfaceProvenance: SPEC §16 documents how the guide itself was generated, which is the most authoritative confirmation of the discovery surface in any of the three PDFs.

alwaysOnFilters._note: One per model, and they are DIFFERENT. Recorded separately for exactly that reason. Do not carry one model's filter to the other.

slsForecastingMetricsExpanded.rule: EXACTLY ONE deduplication filter on every query, always. FCST §4 is headed 'CRITICAL: Data Deduplication — Read This First.'
slsForecastingMetricsExpanded.whyItExists: The underlying data has one row per deal per user in the reporting hierarchy. A single $500K opportunity appears for the owning AE, their FLM, the RVP above, and every leader up to the WW President. Without a dedup filter, SUM(Open_Pipe_clc) overcounts by 3x-10x depending on org depth.

scenarios.byFlmOrRvp: GROUP BY User_Name10 WHERE User_Role2 = 'L9 Leader' — no Is_My_Data_clc

slsForecastingMetricsExpanded.mutuallyExclusive: Is_My_Data_clc and User_Name10 are mutually exclusive and must never be combined. Is_My_Data_clc = 1 'MUST NEVER be applied when querying an entire org unit or filtering to someone who is not the current user. Use User_Name10 instead.'

slsSpecialistReporting.rule: Is_Specialist_AE_Covered_Cleaned_clc = TRUE on EVERY query, always, no exceptions.
slsSpecialistReporting.whyItExists: SPEC §4a: 'The dataset contains both specialist-covered and non-specialist opportunities; this filter removes irrelevant records entirely (it is not a hierarchy dedup). It stays even when querying a specific person by name … Verified against live behavior: the Analytics Agent applies it on every generated query.'
slsSpecialistReporting.dealCounts: Any deal count must be COUNT(DISTINCT Opportunity_ID35), never plain COUNT, because one opportunity recurs across Live / Snaps / Specialist Commit and across snapshots.
slsSpecialistReporting.openDeals: Is_Open_Pipe6 = TRUE AND Data_Source_Cleaned_clc = 'Live', applied explicitly even though some measures already embed the logic.
slsSpecialistReporting.personScoping: No Is_My_Data field exists. Use an OR across Specialist_Level_04_User_Name … Specialist_Level_10_User_Name plus Specialist_User_Name, because a person appears at whichever level matches their role.
slsSpecialistReporting.preferSfrOverCore: Always prefer the specialist / SFR-attributed field over the core version.

slsForecastingMetricsExpanded: Filter NULL dimension values out of any result by default.
Always exclude APM_L120 = 'Other' whenever APM L1 is visible in a chart or table.
'True C&C' means Create_Close_Sub_Type1 IN ('Manufactured', 'Organic'); standard Create & Close is just Is_Create_Close = TRUE.

Default timeframe is the current fiscal YEAR, not quarter. Only scope to a quarter when asked.
Prefer the specialist / SFR-attributed field over the core version, always.

additivityClassification._note: FIRST-CLASS PART OF THE CONTRACT, not a footnote. This is one of the two properties the board's rules card is being recast onto (see userDecisions.rulesArgumentRecast).
additivityClassification.whyItIsFirstClass: The Specialist measure catalogue is PHYSICALLY organised into three headed groups: 'Core KPI Measures — Additive (row-level SUM is safe)', 'Historical / Y-o-Y / CAGR Measures — Non-Additive (DO NOT SUM)', and 'Coverage / Attainment / Ratio Measures — Non-Additive (DO NOT SUM)'. The board asserts that comparability rules live in the measure; here is a real layer that publishes that as a structural property of its catalogue. This is stronger evidence than the invented periodType field the board currently uses.
additivityClassification.discoverableLive: Both docs give aggregationType as a property returned by list_semantic_model_calculated_measures and get_semantic_model_metric, so additivity is checkable at runtime rather than only documented in prose.

additiveSumIsSafe.slsForecastingMetricsExpandedNote: FCST does not publish the same physical split. Treat its dollar measures (ACV_clc, Open_Pipe_clc, Pipe_Gen_clc, Attrition_clc, Current_Commit_clc, Funded_Amount_clc, NNAOV_Commit_clc, Open_Available_to_Renew_clc, Gap_to_Commit_clc, and the Yesterdays_/Last_Weeks_ dollar snapshots) as additive and its ratios as non-additive, but confirm each one's aggregationType live — the classification is inferred for this model, not stated.

additivityClassification.reinforcement: SPEC §12: 'Don't sum ratios — coverage, funded %, velocity, Y/Y, CAGR, averages are non-additive.'

displayConventions.coverage: a MULTIPLIER, not a percent. 2x renders as 2.0. Lowest-coverage rankings must exclude null and negative coverage.
displayConventions.percentages: funded %, Y/Y, CAGR and velocity render as percentages — multiply by 100, append %.
displayConventions.attainment: stored as a decimal 0.0-1.0+. Display: multiply by 100, append %. Filter 'below 80%' as < 0.8, never < 80.
displayConventions.attainmentDomainCompatibility: The [0, 120] fixed attainment domain settled in docs/attainment-encoding.md is directly compatible with the layer's 0.0-1.0+ overrun.

periodToDateComparability._note: FIRST-CLASS PART OF THE CONTRACT, not a footnote. The second of the two properties the board's rules card is being recast onto.
periodToDateComparability.whyItIsFirstClass: Period-to-date semantics exist in this layer as a named, queryable flag, and they exist for exactly the board's reason. This is the single best real-world support for the board's central argument.

Is_QTD_ACV_1_clc.meaning: Is QTD ACV? — original close date within current fiscal QTD. TRUE if ACV is within the QTD window. Use for YoY comparison.

Is_QTD_ACV_clc.meaning: the Specialist model's equivalent QTD flag

AS_OF_YESTERDAY_Was_QTD_ACV_clc.meaning: snapshotted QTD flag as of yesterday

AS_OF_LAST_WEEK_Was_QTD_ACV_clc.meaning: snapshotted QTD flag as of last week

periodToDateComparability.theRule: FCST §5, verbatim: 'Without Is_QTD_ACV_1_clc, you compare a partial current quarter against a full prior quarter, making current year look artificially behind.'
periodToDateComparability.theStockVersusFlowSentence: SPEC §5, verbatim: 'ACV needs PTD for a fair same-end-day comparison; use ACV_PTD_YY_clc. Open Pipe does not require PTD.' That IS the stock-versus-flow distinction, expressed as a query rule rather than as a metadata property. ACV accumulates across a period, so a partial period must be windowed to be comparable. Open Pipe is a balance read at a point in time, so it needs no windowing.
periodToDateComparability.whereTheBoardPutsItWrong: There is NO periodType property on a measure in this layer. The distinction is expressed as (a) the presence or absence of a PTD flag and (b) prose. So the rules card should say 'the layer publishes period-to-date flags and an additivity classification, and refuses the comparison without them' rather than 'the measure declares whether it is a stock or a flow.' The first is true, checkable, and nearly as strong.
periodToDateComparability.verifyPeriodType: REWRITTEN from the previous version of this file. Before plotting any partial period: confirm whether the measure has a PTD flag. If it does, the measure is a flow and the flag is MANDATORY on any cross-period comparison. If the docs explicitly exempt it — as they do for Open Pipe — it is a balance, must not be annualised, and must not be given a PTD window either. If neither is documented, resolve it live via get_semantic_model_metric (aggregationType, isCumulative) and record the finding rather than assuming.
periodToDateComparability.semiAdditiveBehaviour: The layer does not use the term, but the snapshot measures behave as semi-additive balances: Yesterdays_*, Last_Weeks_*, Open_Pipe_PY_clc, Was_Historical_Open_Pipe_clc. The clearest tell is FCST's dead-deal rule: 'How much pipeline was deaded yesterday?' resolves to SUM(Yesterdays_Open_Pipe_clc), because dead deals are $0 in current Open Pipe. A balance that goes to zero the moment its underlying row terminates, requiring a prior snapshot to measure the loss, is a semi-additive measure with a snapshot escape hatch — and the layer ships both the hazard and the escape hatch, named.

dateAnchors.rule: Do not hand-roll date math — use the calculated date fields. FCST adds: never use DATE_TRUNC for historical comparisons, use the pre-calculated relative year fields.
dateAnchors.crossingThemIsAnError: A deal created in Q1 that closes in Q3 is Q1 Pipe Gen but Q3 Open Pipe / ACV. Anchoring pipegen on close date gives the wrong quarter AND the wrong year; anchoring ACV or pipeline on Stage 2 Flag Date is the same error inverted.

calculatedFields.Close_Date_Relative_Year_clc: 'CY' = FY27, 'PY' = FY26, 'PY-1' = FY25, 'Other' = outside the window and typically excluded.

fiscalCalendar.theRelativeYearWindowIsThreeYearsWide: Close_Date_Relative_Year_clc spans CY, PY and PY-1 only. Everything else is 'Other' and typically excluded. RESOLVED BY THE MODEL OWNER, and it is worse than a vocabulary limit: 'Correct, only 3 years of ACV data.' THREE YEARS IS THE ACTUAL EXTENT OF THE DATA, not a naming convention that a cleverer date filter gets around. This file previously recorded it as <TBD: how to source fiscal years beyond PY-1> and treated it as a documentation hole to be chased down. It is not a hole. There is nothing behind PY-1 to reach. An absolute date filter on Close_Date17 for FY23 or FY24 would return no ACV rows, not hand-rolled-but-correct ones, so the discouragement against hand-rolled date math is now beside the point rather than the obstacle. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THAT THE FIVE YEAR TREND TAB CANNOT BE SOURCED — see gaps.fiveYearTrendTabCannotBeSourced, which is the single most material finding produced by the model owner's answers.
fiscalCalendar.theBoardsPeriodLabelIsWrongOnThisCalenda: data/board.json is labelled 'Q2 FY27' with generatedAt 2026-09-01. On the real fiscal calendar, September 1 2026 sits inside FY27 Q3 (FQ3 = August-October). A board labelled Q2 FY27 and generated on Sep 1 is either a closed-quarter retrospective — in which case the QTD flags are unnecessary and any 'quarter to date' kicker is wrong — or it is mislabelled. RESOLVE BEFORE GOING LIVE. See switchOverProcedure.

historicalIsADefinedWindow.definition: FCST §8, verbatim: "'Historical' = average of the same fiscal quarter across the prior 2 fiscal years (PY + PY-1). Not last quarter. Not just last year. Always requires Close_Date_Relative_Year_clc IN ('CY', 'PY', 'PY-1') to return non-null values."
historicalIsADefinedWindow.consequence: Every Historical_* measure is that two-year same-quarter average. It is NOT the board's 'prior year' and must not be labelled as one. A missing 'PY-1' produces nulls rather than an error.
historicalIsADefinedWindow.boardImpact: The 'hist' benchmarks on outlook-matrix (Velocity 17% hist, Coverage 2.7x hist, 2.8x hist) map onto these measures, which means the board's authored description of them as 'the same day of the prior quarter' is wrong: they are a two-year same-quarter average. Either relabel or source a genuine prior-quarter same-day benchmark, which neither document describes.

rowLevelSecurity.queryInheritsTheCallersEntitlementNotThe: The most operationally dangerous property in the whole layer. PULSE states it best: 'Both SDMs enforce row-level security scoped to the CALLER (whoever's Salesforce credentials are connected), not the subject. If Slackbot is running as John Stiefeling and John's entitled hierarchy doesn't include Alfano's org, the queries will return John's data SILENTLY. Verify by checking if returned pipe numbers are in the right magnitude.'
rowLevelSecurity.failureMode: A plausible number for the wrong person. Not an error, not an empty result.
rowLevelSecurity.onlyDocumentedDefence: A magnitude sanity-check. PULSE gives a concrete threshold for its own case ('under $10M for a President org' means abandon and fall back to Org62). Any live board must carry an equivalent PORTLET-SPECIFIC expected-magnitude check and fail loudly rather than render. Record each portlet's expected magnitude band before the first live run.
rowLevelSecurity.neverCallANumberGlobal: Both primary documents require the same caveat on any published output: never present RLS-scoped results as global. meta.scope must say WHOSE ENTITLEMENT produced the numbers, and the provenance face should surface it. This is arguably a better provenance story than the board's invented one, because it is a real constraint with a real failure mode.
rowLevelSecurity.theAuthoredRlsStringIsWrong: board.json's rls string 'Analytics BU hierarchy — viewer sees only their branch' has the wrong subject. Scope is the caller's entitled hierarchy, not a business unit. 'Analytics Business Unit' is not a scope that exists in either model.

They have been removed from guardrails here.

guardrails.neverHardcodeIdentifiers: No SDM apiName, SDM id, workspace id, dashboard id, metric apiName, calculated-field apiName or datasource LUID may be hardcoded from memory or copied from a previous version of this file, from data/board.json, from the sibling app's catalog, or from a prior run. Every one must come from a live list_* / search_assets / get_* call in the runtime environment, every run. This applies even to the two identifiers in this file that look concrete — Sls_Specialist_Reporting's id 2SMed000001kPXVGA2 and the c4e2cc15 LUID prefix. The apiNames quoted from the PDFs are the best available starting point for a discovery search, not a substitute for one.
guardrails.neverInventAnApiName: If docs/semantic-layer.md does not definitively state an apiName, it is written here as <TBD: ...>. Do not complete a truncated apiName from the source PDFs by reconstruction — several deal-movement flag names run past the right edge of the source tables and are cut. Resolve any that a portlet actually needs via list_semantic_model_calculated_measures.
guardrails.pickOneModelPerPortlet: A portlet may source from Sls_Forecasting_Metrics_Expanded or Sls_Specialist_Reporting, never both. They are different populations measured differently, there is no relationship joining them, and no number from one reconciles to a number from the other.
guardrails.verifyGrainBeforeComparing: State BOTH grains, because the gap between them is what the dedup rule exists to close. The PHYSICAL row grain is one row per metric per opportunity per user (Forecasting) or one row per opportunity-line per data source per snapshot (Specialist). The PRESENTATION grain is whatever the utterance groups by. No portlet's authored grain in board.json states either correctly.
guardrails.verifyAdditivityBeforeSumming: See queryContract.additivityClassification. Confirm aggregationType live. Summing a ratio produces nonsense with no error.
guardrails.verifyPeriodTypeBeforePlotting: See queryContract.periodToDateComparability.verifyPeriodType. This replaces the previous version of this file's verifyPeriodType, which asserted a periodType property that does not exist.
guardrails.rlsIsNotOptionalAndIsScopedToTheCaller: See queryContract.rowLevelSecurity. Results are scoped to the caller's entitled hierarchy, not the subject's and not a business unit's. A query run under a service identity will not match what a viewer sees, and the difference will look like a data bug rather than a permissions one — or worse, will not look like anything at all.
guardrails.magnitudeSanityCheckBeforeRendering: Every portlet needs an authored expected-magnitude band. A number 3-10x too large means a missing dedup filter. A number far too small means RLS returned the caller's slice, not the subject's. Both render happily.
guardrails.failLoudlyOnTruncation: A silently truncated result still draws, and still looks right. acv-ae-fan at 1,000 rows is the exposed case. Request the full result set in the utterance and fail loudly if the response is capped.
guardrails.noCredentialsInThisFile: This file holds query shapes, apiNames and field captions only. It must never contain tokens, secrets or connection strings.

portlets._note: One entry per portlet across all five tabs. 27 total. Status values: 'sourceable' (a certified measure exists and the whole tile can be produced), 'partial' (something exists but at a different definition, population or grain, or part of the tile cannot be produced), 'unsourceable' (nothing in either documented model answers this), 'narrative' (authored content, not a query). Every identifier the documents do not state is a <TBD: ...>. No apiName below is invented. Where a portlet is 'partial' or 'unsourceable', `supplementedBy` records what supplies the missing part instead — the source kind, what specifically comes from there, the section of docs/semantic-layer.md that establishes the gap, and what the substitution costs. That field is the operational half of the finding: the board is not a semantic-layer-only artefact and was never going to be, so a gap is only half a fact until it says what fills it. Source kinds: 'google-sheet' (a person maintains it, re-versioned without history), 'warehouse-table' (a system maintains it, refreshed on its own schedule, no enforced as-of date), 'derived-in-board' (a real governed field with an authored grouping over it), 'not-a-source-gap' (the portlet is 'partial' for a reason that is not a missing source — a query-construction rule to keep, or authored narrative — and nothing supplements it).

supplemented.note: Four portlets are supplemented end to end and have no certified counterpart at all; the rest are certified measures with one channel, dimension or period outside the layer. The four are the control group on the direct-to-source toggle: their figures do not move, because there is no guarantee to withdraw.

Left out of the model, it is exactly the kind of definition that gets reimplemented slightly differently by every analyst who needs it: one tests 'Public Sector', one tests 'Pub Sec', one forgets ESMB, one applies the coalesce and one filters instead, and four segment breakouts that all look right disagree — with no error anywhere and no way to tell from the output which one is the house number. Put it in the model once and every consumer inherits the same answer, including the Analytics Agent, which generates SQL from apiNames and cannot infer a rule that lives in someone's workbook. That is the board's own thesis about business vocabulary needing somewhere shared to live, and it arrived unprompted from the person who owns the model rather than from the board arguing for itself. stockExemplarReanchoredToOpenPipe.decision: The stock-versus-flow example is re-anchored FROM AOV ONTO OPEN PIPE.
stockExemplarReanchoredToOpenPipe.whyItWorks: SPEC §5, verbatim: 'ACV needs PTD for a fair same-end-day comparison; use ACV_PTD_YY_clc. OPEN PIPE DOES NOT REQUIRE PTD.' The docs explicitly exempt Open Pipe from period-to-date windowing, which is the stock-versus-flow distinction stated as a query rule. ACV accumulates across a period, so a partial period must be windowed to be comparable. Open Pipe is a balance read at a point in time, so it needs no windowing. Unlike AOV, Open Pipe is a real, governed, queryable measure in BOTH models.
stockExemplarReanchoredToOpenPipe.stockExemplarQueryShape: Return Open Pipe (Open_Pipe_clc) for <scope filter>, filtered to Close_Date_Fiscal_Quarter_Datepart_clc = <resolved at runtime> and Close_Date_Relative_Year_clc = 'CY'. Do NOT apply Is_QTD_ACV_1_clc — Open Pipe is a balance and does not require period-to-date treatment. Do not apply Is_Current_Quarter_clc. Apply exactly one dedup filter.
stockExemplarReanchoredToOpenPipe.priorYearComparison: Open_Pipe_PY_clc is a prior-year open-pipe SNAPSHOT and is the balance-appropriate comparison: a balance is compared to the same balance at a prior point, not windowed to a partial period. Alternatively group Open_Pipe_clc by Close_Date_Relative_Year_clc IN ('CY','PY') — but note that grouping a balance by relative year is comparing two point-in-time reads, and the utterance should say so.
mustNotDo: annualise it — a balance doubled is a number twice its real size that looks like the correct operation
apply a PTD flag to it — the docs explicitly exempt it
SUM Open_Pipe_YY_clc or Open_Pipeline_2_Year_CAGR_clc — both are non-additive
stockExemplarReanchoredToOpenPipe.theDeadDealCaveat: Open_Pipe_clc is $0 for a deal that has been deaded. A balance that goes to zero the moment its underlying row terminates is semi-additive, and the loss is only visible through Yesterdays_Open_Pipe_clc or Last_Weeks_Open_Pipe_Amount_clc. The layer ships both the hazard and the escape hatch, named — which makes Open Pipe a RICHER stock exemplar than AOV would have been, not a weaker one.
stockExemplarReanchoredToOpenPipe.nowMandatoryNotPreferable: The model owner confirms AOV is not available in this SDM, which removes the last alternative. This decision is no longer a choice between two workable options; it is the only one.
stockExemplarReanchoredToOpenPipe.butTheHostTabHasItsOwnCeiling: Whatever replaces trend-aov lands on a tab that can only show three years (gaps.fiveYearTrendTabCannotBeSourced). Open Pipe is a real governed balance, so the stock-versus-flow ARGUMENT is intact — it is made by the contrast between a measure that needs a period-to-date flag and one the docs exempt from it, and that contrast is visible at any number of periods. But an Open Pipe panel drawn across five periods would fail for the same reason the ACV panel does. switchOverProcedure: 0. DISCOVERY FIRST, ALWAYS. None of this board's SDM ids, workspace ids, dashboard ids or datasource LUIDs are knowable in advance. Run list_semantic_models, search_assets and list_workspaces live before any query, even for the two identifiers in this file that look concrete (2SMed000001kPXVGA2 and the c4e2cc15 LUID prefix). Treat every apiName quoted from the PDFs as a discovery starting point, not a substitute for discovery.

1. CONFIRM THE MCP SERVER SURFACE. Verify the Tableau Next MCP server is connected and healthy, and READ THE PARAMETER NAMES OFF ITS OWN TOOL SCHEMA. Three artifacts spell the analyze_data target parameters three different ways and at most one is right. MCP credentials and configuration live entirely outside this repo and are never referenced here.

2. RESOLVE THE FISCAL CALENDAR ISSUE BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE. The real fiscal year starts February 1, so FQ3 = August-October. A board labelled 'Q2 FY27' with generatedAt 2026-09-01 IS DATED INSIDE FY27 Q3. Decide which it is: a closed-quarter Q2 retrospective — in which case the QTD flags are unnecessary and any 'quarter to date' kicker is wrong — or a live Q3 board that is mislabelled. Then resolve Close_Date_Fiscal_Quarter_Datepart_clc AT RUNTIME and never hardcode it; FCST contradicts itself on which quarter is current (header and §11 say Q2, §5 says 3, PULSE says 3 throughout) and the disagreement is a staleness artifact, not a schema fact.

Choose one of: APM_L120 = 'Analytics' (a product scope), an OU_Group_clc / OU_Operating_Unit value (an org scope), or a named leader's hierarchy. These are three different populations and they will not agree. Record the decision, state it on the board, and make it once — if different portlets use different scopes, every cross-tab measure-identity edge the knowledge graph draws becomes false.

4. DECIDE THE MODEL PER PORTLET, AND NEVER MIX. Two unrelated SDMs, no relationship, same words meaning different numbers. Every portlet gets exactly one model. No portlet's choice is open any more: acv-account-fan was the last one where the Specialist model was a live alternative, and its replacement acv-ae-fan is settled on Sls_Forecasting_Metrics_Expanded because it reconciles to kpi-acv. seg-matrix's is settled: the segment derivation in step 5 only works on Sls_Forecasting_Metrics_Expanded, because Segment10 is the only segment field carrying SMB and the derivation cannot create one.

5. BUILD THE DERIVED SEGMENT DIMENSION, IN THE SEMANTIC LAYER. The board's four segment columns are NOT four values of one native dimension. Per the model owner: PubSec is an OPERATING UNIT, not a segment, and the four-way split is a derived dimension — 'IF OU = Public Sector then OU else segment end'. That single line, quoted verbatim, is the definition. Add it to the SDM as a calculated dimension so every consumer inherits the same answer, including the Analytics Agent, which generates SQL from apiNames and cannot infer a rule that lives in someone's workbook. DO NOT reimplement it client-side in each workbook or app: a one-line rule that determines what 'PubSec' means, left out of the model, gets rebuilt slightly differently by every analyst who needs it, and four segment breakouts that all look right disagree with no error anywhere. THEN CONFIRM THE ONE OUTSTANDING IDENTIFIER: the OU field's apiName is <TBD> and neither documented candidate is confirmed to carry a Public-Sector value — OU_Operating_Unit (Forecasting, no value set documented at all) or OU_Group_clc (Specialist, whose value list shows a truncated 'Pub Se…'). The near-hit and the SMB value are in different models and the models cannot be joined, so this check is the highest-value discovery call on the segment tab: if Forecasting's OU field carries no Public Sector value, the four-column set is blocked again and genuinely this time. Resolve the literal with a distinct-values probe, never from a document. See portlets['seg-matrix'].derivedSegmentDimension. STILL OWED SEPARATELY: the board's own enterprise / commercial / growth tier labels used elsewhere match neither model's vocabulary, and the model owner's answer does not address them; and ESMB, which Segment10 carries and the four columns do not show, needs a stated destination.

6. DECIDE WHAT THE FIVE YEAR TREND TAB SHOWS, BEFORE IT GOES LIVE. THE TAB AS DESIGNED CANNOT BE SOURCED. It draws five periods (FY23, FY24, FY25, FY26, FY27 H1) and the model owner confirms there are only three years of ACV data — 'Correct, only 3 years of ACV data.' Three years is the extent of the data, not of the relative-year vocabulary, so there is no date-filter workaround. Four of the seven metric panels have no measure at all and are confirmed unavailable by the model owner (trend-aov, trend-revenue, trend-ae-capacity, trend-ae-productivity); the other three (trend-acv, trend-attrition, trend-nnaov) reach three of five points. The Y/Y channel reaches two of five and the two-year CAGR channel reaches one of five, because a 2-year CAGR at the earliest available year has no prior basis to compute from. DECIDE ONE OF: (a) re-cut the tab as a three-year trend of the three flow metrics that exist, with FY27 as the period-to-date detached point — the recommendation, and still a defensible chart; (b) hold the tab in mock and label it as such; (c) source the missing years from outside this semantic layer, which is a different project. WHAT IS NOT AVAILABLE is rendering five periods against three years of data and fixing it in the caption — two of the five points would have no source, and a chart with two invented points is the exact failure this board exists to argue against. See gaps.fiveYearTrendTabCannotBeSourced.

7. DECIDE THE PRODUCT-MOTION MAPPING, IN THE OPEN. No motion dimension exists. Commit an explicit, versioned APM-L2-to-motion mapping to this repo, labelled as a mapping THIS BOARD DEFINES rather than one the layer provides. Five portlets depend on it: mix-acv, perf-hierarchy, perf-divergence, seg-matrix, outlook-matrix. acv-ae-fan no longer does — it is keyed on a rep, not a product.

8. READ businessPreferences ON BOTH MODELS AND APPLY THEM. They apply to every generated query whether or not you ask. AND DO NOT LIFT A LITERAL FILTER VALUE OUT OF THEM — the stored 'UP +' string is documentation, not data, and filtering on it returns zero rows with no error. Resolve every filter VALUE with a distinct-values probe instead.

9. CONFIRM EVERY FIELD'S VISIBILITY AND aggregationType BEFORE NAMING IT IN AN UTTERANCE. Several fields the board wants are hidden (SFR_Pipe_Gen_Amount_clc, Coverage_clc in the Specialist model, SFR_ID). A hidden field returns nothing rather than erroring. Coverage_clc is the correct field in one model and hidden in the other.

10. WIRE THE ALWAYS-ON FILTERS PER MODEL, NOT GLOBALLY. Forecasting needs exactly ONE dedup filter chosen from the seven scenarios, or results run 3-10x too large; Is_My_Data_clc and User_Name10 are mutually exclusive. Specialist needs Is_Specialist_AE_Covered_Cleaned_clc = TRUE on every query without exception, plus COUNT(DISTINCT Opportunity_ID35) for any count. Note that if the runtime identity has no forecast record, Is_My_Data_clc becomes a NO-OP THAT RETURNS ALL DATA — an analyst or service identity is the likeliest to hit this.

11. AUTHOR AN EXPECTED-MAGNITUDE BAND PER PORTLET AND FAIL LOUDLY OUTSIDE IT. RLS is scoped to the CALLER, not the subject, and a wrong-scope query returns a plausible number silently. A magnitude sanity-check is the only defence documented anywhere in the three sources.

12. MARK THE UNSOURCEABLE PORTLETS AS UNAVAILABLE RATHER THAN GIVING THEM NUMBERS. Five portlets have no source at all: hc-ae, trend-ae-capacity, trend-ae-productivity, trend-aov, trend-revenue. ALL FIVE ARE NOW CONFIRMED BY THE MODEL OWNER, not inferred from a silent catalogue — 'AOV, Revenue, Headcount, and Headcount-Derived metrics (participation, productivity) are not available in this SDM.' Separately: every plan-attainment figure except kpi-pipegen's has no source, and every FinPlan attainment on outlook-matrix has no source. 13. RELABEL THE MEASURES THAT ARE MISLABELLED. NNAOV_Commit_clc is a COMMIT, not a booked actual, on kpi-nnaov and trend-nnaov. outlook-acv's weighted-outlook definition describes a measure that does not exist; the governed forward measure is Current_Commit_clc. outlook-deals must rank on Open_Pipe_clc, not ACV_clc, because ACV_clc is $0 for an open opportunity. outlook-matrix's 'hist' benchmark is a two-year same-quarter average, not the same day of the prior quarter.

VERIFY THE CROSS-TAB MEASURE IDENTITIES BEFORE DRAWING THE KNOWLEDGE-GRAPH EDGES. kpi-acv / trend-acv HOLDS — both are ACV_clc. kpi-nnaov / trend-nnaov holds but both ends are mislabelled. kpi-attrition / trend-attrition holds on Attrition_clc. hc-ae / trend-ae-capacity has no measure at either end, so the edge cannot be drawn. outlook-acv's edge to kpi-acv MUST NOT BE DRAWN if the tile binds to Current_Commit_clc. An edge asserting an identity the layer does not support is the board making exactly the loose claim it argues against.
